title: XY16 width restoration reloads an overwritten X-writer source
summary: MOSInsertREPSEP now saves the actual 16-bit X value before narrowing and restores it before a full-width reader, without replaying a mutable or arithmetic writer. The unchanged original XY16 -Os LTO input returns 0xD77B on MAME and bsnes-jg at 1200 frames; the preserved baseline returns 0xD3BD on both. Focused MIR, live-flags/hard-stack runtime cases, and the earlier XY16 in-place-memmove gate pass.

prior_work.source_assessment: The live MOSInsertREPSEP::placeIntraBlock implementation and patch 0002 clone LastX16Writer after REP #$10 without checking that its source has not changed. The pre/post pass MIR captures the inserted reload after writes to aliases of its source. The existing Y-index and accumulator-spill repairs have different mechanisms.
prior_work.binary_assessment: The preserved pre-gate clang-23 binary SHA-256 is ff61df1d0569ff3a5cf58a8d67e67c57b5a5fee4024adb2dae5e1b1fbcb7f8d5. Its exact original-source ROM is retained and a rebuild from byte-identical snapshot inputs produced the same ROM SHA-256 cf07749d309debc6a3948022fda2838b966ac7f219dc40be27416b77d473cb39. The compiler version string reports LLVM 23.0.0git and vendor pin 8be0546128a55e78c63ca571d466aa72a782cd36; the September 27 gate receipt records the applied patch-stack identity.
prior_work.decision: This is the first structured record for a distinct stale-source replay introduced by the earlier X high-byte restoration. The carry-pressure record is a scheduler performance issue and only held this as an unisolated observation; the near-Y record repairs a separate Y-index sequence. The June X high-byte report remains historical evidence of its own fixed trigger, while this input exposes a new contract failure in the same restoration routine.
prior_work.repair_reconciliation: September 28 repair rechecked the canonical record, original reports and follow-ups, TODO/upstream summaries, Git history (e6433296 and 2689b74d), patch 0002 and the live pass. The stale-writer implementation remained present; no standalone repair existed. Preserved the pre-edit llc and pass source under build/xy16-x-preserve/baseline. This extends the existing causal record; it does not reopen the earlier high-byte-loss or accumulator-spill defects.

unknowns: The full MOS suites report 179 passes, two unsupported and five opt startup failures from duplicate registration of mos-recover-near-nowrap; those IR tests do not execute MOSInsertREPSEP. No full-suite green claim is made. This repair handles intra-block X preservation and known byte/word hard-stack pushes/pulls. Opaque hard-stack operations and shuffles beyond the 8-bit stack-relative range are diagnosed, rather than assigned an unproved stack layout. Wider performance and cross-block X/Y preservation are outside this validation. Standalone parsing of the original MIR rejects mos-static stack IDs; the normalized replay is explicitly derived evidence, while the original C and baseline stay immutable.

resolution.change: patches/llvm-mos/0002-321-accum16.patch: MOSInsertREPSEP::preserveX and pending-narrowing tracking; retained exact implementation in docs/defects/evidence/2026-09-28-xy16-x-preserve/repair.diff
resolution.causal_explanation: PHX saves the value before SEP clears X.high. PLX restores it before a full-width use, even if a Y operation already restored the width. Byte definitions and regmask clobbers end the old X lifetime. Where NZ is live or original stack bytes surround the spill, stack-relative moves preserve A/P and the original byte/word pushes and pulls while removing the saved X word. The overwritten $rs1 source is never reread.
resolution.trigger_check: The same retained C source/header and XY16 -Os LTO configuration fail on the preserved pre-gate compiler and pass on the identified installed candidate. The focused overwritten-source MIR fails FileCheck on the preserved pre-edit llc and passes with this change. A separate flags/stack MIR object executes 32 repetitions with default, A16 and XY16 C callers on both emulators. Original pre-pass MIR is also replayed after only normalizing unsupported mos-static frame metadata; all machine instructions remain unchanged.

candidate.configuration_note: The baseline term pre-gate denotes its ungated computed-carry preference. The candidate explicitly selects mos-carry-sched=always in both Clang and LTO; the original ROM is byte-identical to the candidate built with its default always policy.
